Pension Credit Week of Action from 12 to 16 October 2026

16. This October, we’re running Pension Credit Week of Action to challenge some of the common misconceptions that stop people claiming Pension Credit. Many people mistakenly believe that owning a home, having savings or receiving a private pension automatically makes them ineligible. It doesn’t.

17. As a result, many people of State Pension age who could be entitled to Pension Credit never make a claim.

18. Here are some of the myths we’re tackling this year.

Myths:

own your home? You may still be eligible for Pension Credit. Home ownership is not taken into account when entitlement is calculated

have savings? You could still qualify if you have savings. The first £10,000 of savings is ignored. For every £500 of savings above £10,000, DWP assumes you have an extra £1 a week in income when calculating your Pension Credit entitlement

receive State Pension? Pension Credit is paid in addition to your State Pension and could provide extra financial support

think it happens automatically? Pension Credit is not paid automatically. People need to check their eligibility and make a claim

19. We’re asking stakeholders to help spread these important messages by sharing leaflets that will feature in our TV advert with employees, residents, service users and stakeholders, putting up a poster, sharing posts from the official DWP Facebook channel on social media or creating and sharing your own video content featuring the leaflet.

20. By sharing this information, you could encourage someone to check their eligibility and access support they may otherwise miss out on.

21. To find out more about Pension Credit and how to apply, visit:

Pension Credit – What you’ll get

Pension Credit – How to claim

22. To request printed A5 leaflets and A4 posters (due to be dispatched the week commencing 5 October 2026), please email chiltonmannion.jobshare@dwp.gov.uk.

Practitioners’ Operational Group and Local Authority Welfare Steering Group

23. The last Local Authority Welfare Steering Group meeting took place on 17 September 2026. Agenda items included Legacy Housing Benefit (HB) discovery, bringing together the administration of pensioner HB and Pension Credit, LA funding update and supported housing.

24. Both groups’ meetings are held bi-monthly (and alternately), so the next Practitioner’s Operational Group meeting is scheduled to take place on 15 October 2026.

25. If you have any questions regarding topics raised at these consultation groups, email lawelfare.correspondence@dwp.gov.uk.

HB Decisions by the Upper Tribunal

26. Decision Making and Appeals (DMA) Leeds is aware of the following HB case that has been decided by the Upper Tribunal (UT):

UA-2023-000852-HB: This appeal concerns the Appellant’s entitlement to HB between 25 May 2020 and 7 August 2020. The Appellant is a citizen of the Czech Republic and was lawfully present in the United Kingdom as an EU migrant worker. The judge concluded that the discrimination was not justifiable in this instance

27. You can read all Decisions of the UT on their website. Do be aware that there is an undefined time lapse between decisions being issued and their appearance on the website.

HB cases awaiting decision by the UT

28. DMA Leeds has not been made aware of any case that is awaiting decision by the UT since our previous LA Welfare Direct entry in September 2026.

29. If you have any queries about appeals before the UT Judges or courts, contact us by email at quarryhouse.dmaleedscustomersupportservices@dwp.gov.uk.
